article_title: Modelling diffusion in computer-supported collaborative learning: a large scale learning analytics study
citation: Saqr, M., & López-Pernas, S. (2021). Modelling diffusion in computer-supported collaborative learning: a large scale learning analytics study. Intern. J. Comput.-Support. Collab. Learn. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11412-021-09356-4
title: Dataset of 69 Qassim University PBL course offerings with coded forum interactions
description: An integral Moodle forum dataset of all collaborative-module courses at Qassim University between 2013 and 2019, comprising "69 course offerings (15 different courses)" with "3,277 students" and "97,173 total interactions (of which 8,818 were manually coded)". Posts were coded with an adapted Visschers-Pleijers scheme (Questioning, Information discussion, Argument and debate, Procedural, Off-task), reaching a final Cohen's Kappa of 0.91. Each course grade combined an 80% final exam with forum engagement, continuous assessment and PBL group components.
requirements: courses with at least 30 students were included to satisfy the central limit theorem for the correlation meta-analysis
target_learners: undergraduate healthcare students in problem-based learning courses
target_learning_goals: collaborative problem-solving and argumentation in online PBL forums
examples: All 69 offerings were included to avoid selection or publication bias across several academic years
key_sources: Saqr, M., & López-Pernas, S. (2021). Modelling diffusion in computer-supported collaborative learning: a large scale learning analytics study. Intern. J. Comput.-Support. Collab. Learn. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11412-021-09356-4

article_title: QASEE: A Potential Learning Model to Improve the Critical Thinking Skills of Pre-Service Teachers with Different Academic Abilities
citation: Saputri, W., Corebima, A. D., Susilo, H., & Suwono, H. (2020). QASEE: A potential learning model to improve the critical thinking skills of pre-service teachers with different academic abilities. European Journal of Educational Research, 9(2), 853-864. https://doi.org/10.12973/eu-jer.9.2.853
title: QASEE learning model (Questioning, Answering, Sharing, Extending, Evaluating)
description: QASEE is a constructivism-based learning model designed to develop pre-service teachers' thinking skills through constructive experiential learning. Its five-phase syntax moves students from individually generating questions about unread material, to independently searching for answers, to group sharing with class presentations, to applying knowledge to new real-world contexts, and finally to independent self-evaluation. The article positions QASEE as extending the RQA model by adding group work, knowledge transfer, and self-reflection phases that RQA lacks.
requirements: Students prepare questions and answers individually before class, requiring adequate prior reading of the learning material
constraints: Effectiveness was tested over only one semester, so participants seemed unfamiliar with the model's implementation
target_learners: pre-service teachers in teacher education programs
examples: In the study, three parallel classes of pre-service biology teachers were taught with QASEE, RQA, or conventional learning for one semester
key_sources: Saputri, W., Corebima, A. D., Susilo, H., & Suwono, H. (2020). QASEE: A potential learning model to improve the critical thinking skills of pre-service teachers with different academic abilities. European Journal of Educational Research, 9(2), 853-864. https://doi.org/10.12973/eu-jer.9.2.853

article_title: QASEE: A Potential Learning Model to Improve the Critical Thinking Skills of Pre-Service Teachers with Different Academic Abilities
citation: Saputri, W., Corebima, A. D., Susilo, H., & Suwono, H. (2020). QASEE: A potential learning model to improve the critical thinking skills of pre-service teachers with different academic abilities. European Journal of Educational Research, 9(2), 853-864. https://doi.org/10.12973/eu-jer.9.2.853
title: QASEE five-phase lesson syntax combining individual preparation, group sharing, transfer, and reflection
description: The QASEE syntax structures a lesson cycle in five phases: questioning, answering, sharing, extending, and evaluating. Individual questioning and answering before class build initial knowledge; sharing uses group discussion in which higher-ability students act as tutors; extending applies understanding to new real-world contexts; evaluating is written self-reflection. The article reports this combination gave space for thinking through questions, cooperative groups, oral presentations, authentic activities, and written reflections.
requirements: Each phase must be implemented in sequence, with questioning and answering completed before class begins
constraints: The article notes the model requires students to become accustomed to its various activities over repeated implementation
examples: Upper academic ability students served as tutors for middle and lower ability peers during the sharing phase group discussions
key_sources: Saputri, W., Corebima, A. D., Susilo, H., & Suwono, H. (2020). QASEE: A potential learning model to improve the critical thinking skills of pre-service teachers with different academic abilities. European Journal of Educational Research, 9(2), 853-864. https://doi.org/10.12973/eu-jer.9.2.853

article_title: Development and validation of the QASSH scale: a tool for assessing the quality of simulation scenarios in healthcare education.
citation: Rivière E, Der Sahakian G, Tremblay M-L, Chiniara G. (2025). Development and validation of the QASSH scale: a tool for assessing the quality of simulation scenarios in healthcare education. Medical Education Online. https://doi.org/10.1080/10872981.2025.2486971
title: QASSH — Quality Assessment of Scenarios in Simulation in Healthcare checklist
description: QASSH is a dichotomous (present/absent) checklist for assessing the quality of healthcare simulation scenario scripts before deployment. It "consists of a global section applicable to all simulation modalities and one section that is specific to each of the simulation modalities", with 24 global items in four categories and 10 (immersive, procedural) or 11 (SP) specific items, for total scores of 34 or 35. It functions as three distinct instruments, one per modality.
requirements: Raters should have experience in instructional design for simulation-based education, though novices can use it to guide scenario design
constraints: Developed in French with all raters from the francophone SoFraSimS network; linguistic and cultural idiosyncrasies may limit use in other settings, and English-version equivalence needs further research
All validation raters were experts in SBE, so results may not generalize to raters without such expertise
target_learners: Healthcare professionals in pre- and post-graduate simulation-based education
target_learning_goals: Assessing and improving the educational quality of simulation scenario scripts for immersive simulation, procedural simulation and simulated participants
examples: Raters used QASSH to independently assess a gunshot wound scenario (immersive), a lumbar puncture scenario (procedural) and a bad-news communication scenario (SP), each at low, borderline and high designed quality levels
key_sources: Rivière E, Der Sahakian G, Tremblay M-L, Chiniara G. (2025). Development and validation of the QASSH scale: a tool for assessing the quality of simulation scenarios in healthcare education. Medical Education Online. https://doi.org/10.1080/10872981.2025.2486971
